title: Client prefetch simulation and hypothesis lab
content:
Goal:
Quick, messy lab notes for an experiment framework to reason about client-side prefetch heuristics and their interaction with Redwood runtime batching/caching. Not a product spec yet — trying to capture intuitions, small API sketches, a micro-simulator, and telemetry hooks to validate hypotheses.

Context / motivations:
- Many user flows see bursts of short requests followed by quiet periods (chat UIs, interactive shells).
- Prefetching next-turn prompts or likely continuations can reduce perceived latency but increases token cost and may pollute caches.
- Redwood runtime has prefix/KV caching and continuous batching; prefetch decisions interact nontrivially with those systems.
- Want a lightweight, client-configurable policy layer that: can be simulated offline, produces explainable telemetry, and fits into the existing client SDKs.

High-level hypotheses:
1) Conservative prefetch (threshold-based confidence + token budget cap) -> lower median latency for interactive apps with <10% token overhead.
2) Aggressive prefetch with tenant-aware throttling improves p95 only for high-reuse prompts but increases cost for multi-tenant workloads.
3) Prefetch that is KV-aware (prefetch only when cache miss probability > X) provides best win/cost tradeoff.

Important constraints:
- Any client policy must be opt-in by default and respect tenant token budgets.
- Must avoid prefetching for requests with sensitive inputs unless explicitly allowed.
- Policies should be configurable via small DSL or JSON config to enable remote tuning.

Sketch: client prefetch policy API shape (informal)
- We want an API that is small, serializable, and easy to run in the browser or a small server.
- Example shape (pseudo-JSON):
  {
    "policy_name": "threshold-v0",
    "confidence_threshold": 0.7,            // model-side or client-estimated probability that a given continuation will be used
    "max_prefetch_tokens": 64,              // budget per session/minute
    "cooldown_ms": 1200,                    // do not prefetch more often than this
    "kv_awareness": {"enabled": true, "cache_miss_prob_threshold": 0.4},
    "telemetry_sample_rate": 0.02            // fraction of prefetches that emit full debug traces
  }

Prefetch flow (client):
- on user action (partial input, keystroke pause, explicit next-turn intent):
  1) consult policy -> decide prefetch vs skip.
  2) if prefetch: create a lightweight prefetch request with tag prefetch=true, prefetch_reason, and prefetch_id.
  3) send to Redwood endpoint with header X-Redwood-Prefetch: 1 and optionally X-Redwood-Prefetch-Id.
  4) Redwood runtime treats tagged prefetch requests as low-priority: they can be batched into low-latency windows or queued for best-effort execution depending on tenant config.
  5) if later the user actually issues the request that matches the prefetch_id, billing is adjusted (dedupe semantics) — see billing notes below.

Billing/dedupe semantics (draft):
- If prefetch returned tokens T_pref and a subsequent user request reuses the same prefix/cache entry within TTL, then charge only the incremental tokens beyond the cached prefix.
- If prefetch generated a fully-materialized response that matches user request exactly, apply a credit (negative charge) to offset the earlier prefetch cost — requires deterministic matching and strong hashing.
- Simpler interim rule: prefetch tokens billed normally but flagged in telemetry; use aggregate cost analysis to decide policies.

Server-side tagging/heuristics (runtime notes):
- Add header/metadata: prefetch:true|false, prefetch_id, confidence_hint, client_policy_hash.
- Runtime should expose per-tenant counters: prefetch_count, prefetch_serve_rate, prefetch_cache_hit_rate, prefetch_cost_tokens.
- Batching: allow runtime to group prefetches into separate low-priority queues that only run when GPU utilization < X, or run in dedicated short bursts.

Micro-simulator plan (local):
- Simulator models:
  - client arrival process (Poisson or real traces replay),
  - user-turn selection probability (probability that a prefetch candidate is actually used),
  - model response length distribution,
  - cache TTL and hit/miss probabilities as a function of time and prefix reuse,
  - cost per token and latency distribution (cold vs warm, batched vs dedicated).
- Inputs: small corpus of UI traces (we can synthesize using our telemetry samples), policy configs, runtime config knobs (batch window ms, low-priority queue cap).
- Outputs: per-policy metrics: avg perceived latency (time to first useful token), token overhead, p95 latency, GPU utilization, cache hit rate, cost per 1k sessions.

Example experiment matrix:
- Vary confidence_threshold = [0.5, 0.7, 0.9]
- max_prefetch_tokens = [16, 64, 256]
- kv_awareness.enabled = [false, true] and cache_miss_prob_threshold = [0.1, 0.4, 0.7]
- arrival patterns: chat-like (bursty), command-line (short bursts very frequent), slow-form (infrequent long requests)

Telemetry events (minimal + debug):
- prefetch.requested {prefetch_id, policy_hash, reason, tokens_requested}
- prefetch.completed {prefetch_id, tokens_returned, cache_entry_hash}
- prefetch.matched {prefetch_id, user_request_id, dedupe_type}
- prefetch.evicted {prefetch_id, reason}
- sampling: capture full model trace for 1% of prefetches for offline analysis

ASCII diagram (very rough):
  [Client] --prefetch(req,prefetch_id)--> [Edge LB] --> [Runtime low-prio queue] --runs when util<80%--> [GPU pool / KV cache] // returns prefetch tokens cached
  ..later..
  [Client] --real req + prefetch_id--> [Runtime] --cache hit?--> serve from cache (cheap)

Open design questions / risks:
- Privacy: prefetching user input that includes PII — how to ensure opt-in, redaction, and client-side policy enforcement?
- Billing complexity: dedupe requires either deterministic matching or a reconciliation pipeline to issue credits; both add complexity for little incremental value early on.
- Cache pollution: prefetch might evict hot entries for other tenants in shared caches. Need tenant-aware eviction or strict tenant isolation for prefetch cache entries.
- Cold-start behavior: prefetching on cold models wastes tokens if model warmup is expensive. Might want to prefer prefetch only when model warm or when using model variant with cheap token cost.

Next steps (short):
- Build simple Python simulator (timeline: 1-2 weeks) that can run the experiment matrix on synthetic traces.
- Add minimal prefetch headers support to edge (instrumentation only) behind feature flag (SRE + infra review).
- Run 2-3 A/B simulations with real telemetry samples (anonymized) to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Notes to self / todo:
- Talk to billing about feasibility of credits and deterministic matching requirements (mention: JIRA-RI-4321).
- Draft a tiny client SDK sample (JS) that shows how to enable policy and emits telemetry.
- Check with security on sensitive-input heuristics before enabling auto prefetch in any customer-facing app.

Quick JS client pseudocode (sketch):
  async function maybePrefetch(input, policy) {
    if (!policy.enabled) return;
    if (!passesPrivacyChecks(input)) return;
    const confidence = clientEstimateNextTurnProb(input);
    if (confidence < policy.confidence_threshold) return;
    if (tokenBudgetExceeded(policy.max_prefetch_tokens)) return;
    const prefetchId = uuid();
    const headers = {
      "X-Redwood-Prefetch": "1",
      "X-Redwood-Prefetch-Id": prefetchId,
      "X-Client-Policy": policy.policy_name
    };
    emitTelemetry('prefetch.requested', {prefetchId, policy});
    fetch('/v1/generate', {method: 'POST', headers, body: buildPrefetchBody(input, policy.max_prefetch_tokens)});
  }

Appendix: random thought collection (short bullets)
- Could we use a tiny local ranker to predict which prompt continuation to prefetch (small CLM on-device)?
- Maybe prefetch only embeddings for retrieval-heavy apps rather than full token generation.
- Consider prefetch as a separate product tier: "prefetch credits" in Dedicated offering where tenants pay for pre-reserved prefetch capacity with stricter isolation.

End of scratchpad.
